ownershipBoundaries.contract: Provider-neutral JSON-schema rendering and reconciliation; provider IDs and vendor URLs are forbidden.
Provider-neutral handoff from a probed provider-owned execution capability into create readiness and instance mapping; local runtime fields remain untouched for non-owning providers.
Provider-neutral channel, team, template, and mention placement through the existing execution-ownership capability; remote placement never requires or persists a desktop runtime projection.

Generic immutable provider staging, transient signed execution-ownership probing, platform lookup, optional signer policy, caller-owned zeroizing request buffers, and provider-confirmed hosted-agent deletion before local state is removed.
Provider-neutral, fail-closed DM recipient hydration with no remote or tenant assumptions.
Repository-provider-neutral README normalization.
Provider-neutral TTS message sanitization.

Provider-neutral durable publication and explicit-user cancellation recovery, deterministic signed event identity, and thread-scoped non-chat operational status. Non-chat invocation control cannot create or delete a chat message.
Storage-backend-neutral media behavior with Azure adaptation outside the upstream switch.
Storage-backend-neutral Git object semantics with Azure result translation isolated.
Provider-neutral dispatch of unknown deep-link actions into separately owned extensions; no tenant, vendor, or coordinator assumptions.
Provider-neutral Tauri state and command registration for a separately owned, secret-local identity lifecycle extension.
Provider-neutral rendering seam for a self-contained identity lifecycle dialog with no configured coordinator or tenant knowledge.

Provider-neutral, pre-render migration of exact public identity presentation markers after a natively committed rotation; no secrets, transactions, drafts, or message state cross the identity boundary.

Provider-neutral bounded operational observations and domain-separated, community-bound runtime publication/cancellation authorizations; neither protocol decides semantic completion or successor selection.

Exact issuer trust, scope, receipt and publication fences enforced in the event insertion transaction. Explicit Stop and contribution insertion serialize without rewriting historical contributions or weakening ordinary moderation deletion.

The authenticated generic Nostr query bridge exposes original signed Stop evidence for an exact community/channel/author/thread scope and a writer-only commit-ordered channel event stream. Atomic event-store triggers retain exact Stop commands independently of chat retention and assign exact decimal channel positions without skipping a later-committing event. Neither read acknowledges input or invents runtime admission, outcome, or scheduling policy.

Read-only bounded Stop evidence and commit-ordered channel queries over the existing NIP-98 bridge. Preserve all seven signed fields and exact decimal sequence strings without replaying chat or acknowledging input/cancellation.
Operator-only immutable verification-key provisioning within the explicitly configured relay community; events cannot provision their own authority.

Signed recipient-only invocation wakes, including self-addressed recovery wakes whose signer is also the recipient, and thread-only operational observations use dedicated event kinds, never chat send/delete plumbing.
Strict signer-attributed, plain-text system status inside its own thread, excluded from root chat and conversational unread activity; ordinary chat and moderation rendering remain separate.
The same operational event boundary rendered as thread-scoped system status without answer/edit/delete affordances or a semantic finish decision.

deltas.purpose: Generic onboarding and agent-reliability fixes found while exercising a closed Kiingo relay: keep the relay's rejection reason on a latched-terminal session so onboarding shows membership denial instead of a generic server error; re-sign retained agent heads that aged out of the relay window; stop retrying stale status publications; optionally assert the agent's display name; publish an agent's final text when it ends a channel turn without posting (relay-verified, never double-posts); ignore agent channel messages addressed to another agent; repair missing DM discovery metadata on re-open; open a fresh DM when the opener's membership was revoked (e.g. identity rotation) instead of returning a sealed one; an optional hot-reloaded respond-to allowlist file; NIP-10 parent-author notification for unaddressed CLI replies; an opt-in allowlist-in-DMs rule that admits allowlisted authors only when every DM participant is trusted; and full-access mode mapping so bypassPermissions reaches adapters whose full-access mode has a different id (codex-acp agent-full-access), with a warning when a requested mode is not advertised; and keep relay-signed kind:40099 system events (dm_created) out of the Home inbox DM context, which has no system-row renderer and showed their JSON as chat; and export each agent turn's reply destination (BUZZ_TURN_CONTEXT_FILE) so `buzz messages send` in the turn's channel replies in the triggering thread by default, with --top-level to opt out; and refuse further chat sends to the turn's channel after the agent @mentions someone other than itself and the turn's triggering members (a floor handoff recorded beside the turn file), unless --after-handoff is passed, so an agent cannot ask a question and post the conclusion in the same turn; parallel sends in one turn serialize the handoff check, send, and marker write on an advisory lock file in the turn directory; and carry a saved agent definition's access (who can send instructions) to its deployed instances still on the definition's previous access, through the instance update command so the running agent restarts on the new gate, and let the access people picker add a pasted npub or hex key whatever the profile search returns, with the member picker's search page size; and keep Home inbox thread context failures per message (reuse ancestors already in the channel window, retry a failed context fetch once, render an inline placeholder for a deleted or unreadable root/ancestor and a quiet retry note for replies) instead of a page-level error banner, and refresh channel rosters on every live kind:40099 membership row (joined/left/removed/added) for all member channels, not only the open channel screen, with the members sidebar revalidating a cached roster on open.
deltas.upstreamStatus: Upstream candidates; each fix is self-contained and generic, to be proposed to block/buzz.
deltas.removalCondition: Remove each path once block/buzz ships an equivalent fix.

The read gate now derives from RESULT_GATED_KINDS instead of hard-coded kinds.
deltas.upstreamStatus: Generic notification kinds with no deployment-specific behaviour; not yet proposed upstream.
deltas.removalCondition: Remove when block/buzz ships owner-addressed approval notification kinds with private reads and push eligibility.

deltas.purpose: Cross-owner agent access, harness side: the inbound author gate returns a trust tier (owner, same-owner sibling, guest, other owner's agent) decided from signed data; an optional hosted guest-turn mode (BUZZ_ACP_GUEST_TURNS=hosted, BUZZ_ACP_GUEST_ROUTE_URL) hands every non-owner event, with its thread context, verified relay chain, author profile and audience, to a NIP-98-authenticated guest route instead of the local agent session, publishes the route's outbox verbatim and acknowledges it, and registers the endpoint; the queue's conversation key carries a trust lane so a non-owner event never batches into or steers an owner turn; signed agent-to-agent provenance tags (buzz-relay, buzz-relay-prev, buzz-root-budget, buzz-guest) with per-hop verification and a hop limit of 2, written by `buzz messages send` from the turn's trigger; harness-enforced loop guards (per-pair rate limit, per-root budget, request dedup, echo suppression, no re-asking while approval is pending, no agent p-tags in guest output); a [guest: <name> via <agent>] prompt marker; a DM is addressed to every participant (known DMs subscribe without the #p filter and match without the mention requirement; `buzz messages send` p-tags every other DM member, as the desktop does); in hosted mode, crossing text is withheld from the local session's thread/DM history and guest output never suppresses an owner turn's reply fallback; a live-relay E2E suite; owner-turn sends (and the harness reply fallback) to a shared audience or another owner's agent are classified with the guest route's /classify and published, held for the owner, or dropped; in hosted mode `buzz messages get/thread/search` and `feed` withhold (or, with --show-untrusted, fence as untrusted data) messages from anyone but the owner, this agent and same-owner agents, and all guest output; the guest outbox is drained from startup and right after each registration, continuously, by one process per agent key (advisory lock) with at most one request in flight and a unique NIP-98 nonce per request, on its own HTTP client so routing (/turns, register, classify, on a short-timeout no-reuse control client) never waits on it, cursor-free, item by item (malformed items failed back, transient failures deferred per item), with owner notifications accepted only for this agent's own owner; owner-signed approve/deny guest-reply control frames; and the desktop pinning hosted guest turns (reserved env) with a build-time guest route URL.
deltas.upstreamStatus: Generic mechanism (no deployment-specific endpoints); not yet proposed upstream.
deltas.removalCondition: Remove when block/buzz ships an equivalent trust-tiered gate with an out-of-process guest runtime and agent-to-agent provenance.

deltas.purpose: Owner and guest desktop UX for cross-owner agent access through a hosted guest route. Owner side: a native NIP-98 client for the route's owner and identity endpoints (no browser CORS; agent routes stay with the harness), trusted 46040-46042 owner notifications (accepted only from the owner's own agents, by local ownership or a verified NIP-OA profile) merged into the Inbox like workflow approvals, a pending-approvals poll as the system of record, an approval review dialog (exact draft, requester and link state, venue, data sources, plain-language classifier reasons, edit then approve, owner-data requests that release only the sources the owner picks to one re-run of the guest turn, deny, deny and block, grant scope) that records the decision first and then sends the approve/deny observer control frame, a prominent alert banner, a link-your-account prompt and profile card, and an agent settings Access dialog (policy, grants, requests, blocks, shared items, learned-grant suggestions, daily digest). Guest side: markers on hosted guest replies with pending, resolved and refusal states. Upstream files carry only mount points, inbox labels and a feed merge. Approval cards show who is asking (TEST badge, route-classified kind, linked-ago, first/Nth request), a one-line description of what each shareable source exposes with nothing pre-ticked when the request named none, and a preview sentence above the buttons that follows the owner's current choices; all additive and optional for older routes. Org admins get an agent guest safety card in Settings, Profile, below the account link card (open org-wide alerts with Mark reviewed, and suspended requesters with Restore access) through the route's admin endpoints, which the native client now also reaches. Alert banners route Review by the alert's kind tag: the digest, the agent's requests, the admin card, or nothing for agent-request outcome notices.
deltas.upstreamStatus: Generic mechanism configured by the build-time guest route URL; not yet proposed upstream.
deltas.removalCondition: Remove when block/buzz ships owner review and settings UI for hosted guest turns.

deltas.purpose: Provider-neutral hosted-agent create flow. A build-time VITE_BUZZ_PREFERRED_RUN_ON names a bundled destination: when that provider is discovered, 'Where it runs' leads the create form with exactly that destination (default) or this computer, plain labels, prefilled name and instructions, and no untrusted-binary warning for the provider shipped inside the signed app bundle. Provider protocol v2 gains an optional read-only 'preflight' lifecycle operation (owner-signed kind-27236 proof) so the dialog can show owner readiness, a Connect action and a one-line notice, and block Create until ready. Deploy failures may carry remote_state 'absent'. A failed remote start is rolled back: confirmed delete when an agent id is known, otherwise one replay of the idempotent deploy to learn it; the local record and key are kept unless the provider confirmed deletion or absence. A conditionally shown bounded provider field (x-visible-when with options) must hold a current option before Create, and an empty option list renders an explicit empty state instead of a blank dropdown.
deltas.upstreamStatus: Generic provider protocol and create-flow improvements; candidate for upstream.

deltas.purpose: Mobile owner review of agent guest-access approvals, matching the desktop approval card. Tapping a 46040 request in the Activity inbox opens a review sheet that fetches the approval from the hosted guest route (the system of record) with a native NIP-98 owner client (X-Buzz-Community = active relay host) and shows who is asking (TEST badge, route-classified kind, link state, linked-ago, first/Nth request), the venue, the exact draft, data used and plain-language hold reasons, a sources picker for owner-data requests with nothing pre-ticked when the request named none, a grant scope, and a preview sentence that follows the owner's current choices. Approve / Edit then approve (write the reply myself) / Deny / Deny and block record the decision first, then send the owner-signed NIP-44 observer control frame; a decided request leaves the inbox at once. 46042 alerts open their text. The route is the build-time --dart-define BUZZ_GUEST_ROUTE_URL and is used only while the community it serves (BUZZ_GUEST_ROUTE_RELAY_URL, default BUZZ_RELAY_URL) is active; without it the sheet says to review on desktop. The upstream inbox page carries one open hook.
deltas.upstreamStatus: Generic mechanism configured by the build-time guest route URL; not yet proposed upstream.
deltas.removalCondition: Remove when block/buzz ships owner review of hosted guest-turn approvals on mobile.

deltas.purpose: Mobile creation and management of hosted agents, matching the desktop create flow. The phone has no provider binary, so a native Dart client speaks the same provisioning contract the desktop's bundled provider uses: GET /capabilities (Ed25519 catalog pinned by the build-time key, validity window, API-base check), POST /preflight and POST /agents/confirmed-delete with owner-signed kind-27236 proofs (buzz-provider-preflight-v1 / buzz-provider-delete-v1, exact ordered tags), and POST /agents with the standard NIP-OA owner attestation and an x25519-chacha20poly1305 identity envelope (v2 bundle: key plus attestation) sealed to the catalog's provisioning key. The agent key is generated in memory per create and dropped afterwards; it is never stored. The create form leads with Where it runs, renders the provider schema generically (harness, model mode, model family/version, reasoning, tier) with the desktop's visibility, option-filter, reconcile and unmet-choice rules, gates Create on a fresh ready preflight of the current configuration (re-checked on resume and Check again), and rolls back a failed create (confirmed delete with a known id; otherwise one identical idempotent replay then delete; agent_state absent is the only proof of absence; an unconfirmed cleanup is kept in memory and retried before the next create). On success it publishes the agent's kind:0 (agent NIP-98 plus x-auth-tag) and the owner's kind:30177, and remembers the public record; delete retires both (kind:5 plus NIP-IA 9035). Management uses the owner-key routes POST /owner/agents/list, /owner/agents/update and /owner/agents/control with buzz-provider-owner-v1 proofs (list: 5 tags; writes: 7 tags binding the agent and the SHA-256 of the canonical body), a fresh single-use proof per attempt and a fixed request id for idempotent retries: the Agents page lists every hosted agent with live state (desktop-created included), pauses/resumes, checks status, reconciles, edits name, instructions, harness and model through the same schema form and preflight (a revision conflict refreshes and asks to save again; lifecycle actions retry once on the newest revision), and deletes any of them through confirmed delete plus the desktop's kind:30177 tombstone and NIP-IA archive. The owner's other kind:30177 agents are listed read-only. Configuration is build-time only: BUZZ_HOSTED_AGENTS_URL, BUZZ_HOSTED_AGENTS_CATALOG_KEY, BUZZ_HOSTED_AGENTS_LOCATION and BUZZ_HOSTED_AGENTS_RELAY_URL (default BUZZ_RELAY_URL), gated to the community it serves. Upstream hooks: one optional Settings page builder and row part, the app.dart builder line (app.dart is classified with the push-tap delta), and the pure-Dart cryptography dependency.
deltas.upstreamStatus: Generic mechanism configured entirely by build-time values; not yet proposed upstream.
deltas.removalCondition: Remove when block/buzz ships hosted-agent creation and management on mobile.

deltas.removalCondition: Remove when block/buzz routes channel-less notification taps and exposes an app icon override.

deltas.purpose: Mobile owner management of agent guest access, matching desktop's per-agent Access dialog across all of the owner's agents. Settings shows an Agent guest access row (hidden without a route for the active community or a signing key) that opens: each registered agent's hosted-answer switch (PATCH /owner/agents/{id}); active grants with Revoke; recent requests from the access log with an agent filter, cursor paging, outcome/tier/data-used/safety-check detail and Block; blocked people with Unblock; items shared via my agent with add and Stop sharing; learned-grant suggestions with Allow/Dismiss; the read-only daily digest by UTC day; and, for org admins only (admin_required hides it), the guest safety review with Mark reviewed and Restore access. The existing NIP-98 owner client gains these owner and admin routes as an extension in a part file; no route is added or changed. The upstream settings page (already classified by the hosted-agents delta) carries one section hook.

deltas.purpose: Desktop remote signer (Kiingo design mcp-buzz-module.md section 7): a broker next to the build-time guest route (its /buzz-signer/v1 sibling, or BUZZ_DESKTOP_REMOTE_SIGNER_URL) can ask this device to sign as the user. A Rust long-poller (GET /requests?wait_ms=25000, one request in flight, backoff on errors) runs only while the app runs and the per-device, per-community switch 'Allow Kiingo to request signatures' (off by default) is on; every broker call is NIP-98 signed by the user's key with the guest route's X-Buzz-Community. Each request is validated in the backend before anything is shown: signer and event pubkey are the user's own, the expected event id matches the computed id, relay_url is the connected relay's /events or /query, publish kinds are 9/7/40003/9005 (never 0, 10100, 30315, 9000-9002, 9007, 9008, 9030-9032, 27235, 27236, 24243, 1059, identity-rotation kinds or NIP-OA auth tags), only h/e/p/k tags, the h tag equals the displayed channel, the action matches the kind, edits and deletes target the user's own message, read filters stay within the read kinds, and expired requests are skipped; anything else is declined and never signed. A consent modal shows 'Signing as: You (<name>)' distinct from agents, the locally derived action, the channel resolved locally with member count or DM peer, full content or read scope, kind and the requesting client/agent, with Allow once, Deny and Allow for... (kinds in this channel, or reads in this channel or all channels, for 15 min/1 h/8 h). Scopes are created only from the prompt and stored only in the app data dir (remote-signer.json), auto-approve with decision_source scope:<id>, are listed in Settings, Kiingo signing with per-scope revoke, and a top-chrome pill ('Kiingo can sign as you, N scopes') offers one-click revoke of all. A local signing log records time, action, channel, decision and outcome event id (no signatures). Signing (the exact event plus the relay NIP-98 header over the exact body) happens in Rust; the renderer receives display data only. Upstream files carry a module/command registration, the dialog host mount and the settings section hook.
deltas.upstreamStatus: Generic mechanism configured by the build-time guest route URL; Kiingo naming only in added files; not proposed upstream.
deltas.removalCondition: Remove when block/buzz ships a remote signer (NIP-46 or equivalent) with device-local consent scopes, or when Kiingo moves remote signing to relay-native NIP-46.

deltas.purpose: Exact upstream iOS build fixes needed to archive the Kiingo TestFlight build with Xcode 27.0 (the only Xcode on the release Mac): b270437a (NotificationService clears inherited CocoaPods linker flags; its CI lane change is not taken because fork runners only admit the current workflow), 46159fcf (Podfile raises generated pod deployment targets to iOS 16; lockfile checksum is the SHA-1 of the fork Podfile) and 73962435 (BuzzPushKit signs and verifies Nostr Schnorr signatures through vendored, unmodified Bitcoin Core libsecp256k1 v0.8.0 instead of swift-secp256k1 0.21.1, which Xcode 27 cannot compile).
